The $625 million figure and the Counsel Health acquisition match the real headline. The satire is aimed at the right target (tech hype and clinical AI), and it doesn't mock patients, reporters or private individuals. It doesn't quote the article or touch any excluded topics. Remove or verify the IPO claim, for example by cutting it to 'Oura is spending $625 million on clinical AI', and it should pass.

pick.title: Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, placing a big bet on AI care
pick.headline: Smart Ring Maker Pays $625 Million to Teach Jewelry to Practice Medicine
pick.take: After delaying its IPO, Oura is spending $625 million on clinical AI. The ring that tells you how you slept will now tell you what to do about it. Physicians are still waiting on a prior authorization that no ring, algorithm or fax machine has managed to approve.
